q: 1. An old worn out tyre may offer more friction on a dry surface than a new tyre with treads because .............
options: old surface got more accustomed for the surface of road
new tyre had a smooth surface
old surface had more contact area
hollows of treads of tyre had more friction
explain: On dry surfaces, a smooth (worn out) tyre provides a larger contact area with the pavement, resulting in higher friction compared to a treaded tyre.

q: 2. Unevenness of a pavement should be preferably less than .............
explain: An unevenness index of less than 150 cm/km is considered good for high-speed roads, while values above 250 cm/km indicate poor riding quality.

q: 3. Weight of a vehicle affects the design of .............
options: camber and gradient of a road
pavement thickness and gradient of a road
explain: Pavement thickness is directly designed based on the anticipated axle loads (weight) and the number of repetitions.

q: 4. The layer that is directly coming in contact with the traffic is .............
explain: The wearing course (or surface course) is the topmost layer that resists the abrasion from traffic and provides a smooth riding surface.

q: 5. A pavement is classified as flexible pavement or rigid pavement based on its .............
explain: The distinction is primarily based on the structural action and the material of the top layer (Bituminous for flexible, Concrete for rigid).

q: 6. The first artificial course provided on a highway .............
explain: The sub-grade is natural soil; the sub-base is the first layer of man-made material placed over it to distribute loads.

q: 7. Skidding occurs on ............. pavement.
explain: Skidding occurs when the pavement surface is smooth or slippery (low friction), causing the wheels to slide without rotating.

q: 8. The layer of the road that may not contribute to unevenness is.
explain: The formation is the prepared natural ground. Unevenness is usually a result of poor construction or settlement of the artificial pavement layers above it.

q: 9. Greater unevenness causes .............
explain: High unevenness indices lead to loss of vehicle control, increased fatigue, and vehicle damage, significantly increasing accident risk.

q: 10. A pavement that offers poor visibility is .............
explain: Bituminous (black-top) roads absorb more light, leading to poor visibility at night compared to lighter-colored concrete or gravel roads.

q: 11. A drawback of a rigid pavement is that .............
options: no crack occurs even if local settlement takes place
it acts as a bridge to cover minor depression like irregularity
its ability to withstand iron wheeled traffic is less
explain: Rigid pavements are brittle; once a structural crack (rift) starts due to fatigue or temperature, it tends to propagate and widen quickly.

q: 12. An example of a rigid pavement is .............
explain: Cement concrete roads are the classic example of rigid pavements, where the slab itself provides structural strength through flexural rigidity.

q: 13. When lime is added to a soil, it .............
options: increases grain size due to electrolytic and chemical action
lowers plastic limit and increases liquid limit
explain: Lime causes flocculation of clay particles, effectively increasing the apparent grain size and making the soil more workable.

q: 14. Surface painting is .............
options: marking of white and yellow lines on pavement
providing a thin Bituminous layer over WBM roads
application of Bitumen concrete layer over WBM roads
application of a hot mix of bitumen and then stone chips over it
explain: Also known as surface dressing, it involves spraying hot bitumen followed by a layer of stone chips to provide a wearing surface.

q: 15. A Bitumen Bound Macadam Pavement is best suited where .............
options: ground water table is at shallow depths
the climate is hot and humid
explain: Bitumen Bound Macadam (BBM) is an open-graded premix; it performs best in dry regions (scant rainfall) where drainage through the layer is less of a concern.

q: 16. Seal coat is a layer of .............
options: adhesive to improve bond between aggregates
explain: A seal coat usually consists of a thin application of binder and fine aggregate (coarse sand) to seal the surface.

q: 17. Purpose of the seal coat is to provide .............
explain: The main function of a seal coat is to make the pavement surface impervious to water, preventing it from reaching the base layers.

q: 18. The best road suited to pneumatic and iron wheeled traffic is .............
explain: Cement concrete (rigid) roads are the most durable and can withstand the high abrasive stress caused by iron-wheeled carts without deforming.

q: 19. Cement concrete road can be laid over .............
options: an earthen road subjected to traffic for 1 year
a WBM road of thickness greater than 150 mm and subjected to traffic for 1 month
any black top road is use at least for 2 weeks
explain: A stable WBM base that has been compacted by traffic for at least a month provides a reliable foundation for a concrete slab.

q: 20. Minimum lateral clearance desirable from the pavement edge is .............
explain: For safety and capacity, objects (like poles or trees) should ideally be at least 1.85m away from the edge of the traveled lane.

q: 21. A lamp post at the edge of the pavement reduces the capacity of the lane to .............
explain: Obstacles near the lane edge cause 'lateral clearance' effects where drivers slow down or move away, reducing overall lane capacity to about 83%.

q: 22. In water bound macadam roads, binding material, is .............
explain: WBM roads use stone screenings and stone dust, which—when mixed with water—act as a binder to fill the voids between larger aggregates.

q: 23. Full amount of extra width of a pavement on the curve, is provided at
explain: Widening is introduced gradually along the transition curve and reaches its full value at the start of the circular curve.

q: 24. An ideal pavement is constructed with
explain: Portland Cement Concrete (PCC) is considered ideal for high-durability, long-life pavements with low tractive resistance.

q: 25. In case of cement concrete pavements, pick up the incorrect statement
options: initial cost of construction is high
initial cost of construction is low
explain: Concrete pavements are known for having a high initial construction cost compared to flexible (bituminous) pavements.

q: 26. The basic formula for determination of pavement thickness was first suggested by
explain: Goldbeck provided early simplified formulas for pavement thickness based on wheel loads and allowable stresses.

q: 27. When each particle of aggregates is thinly coated with cement paste, a heterogeneous solid is formed, which is known as
explain: Concrete is a composite material formed by binding aggregates (sand/gravel) together with cement paste.

q: 28. For maximum strength and durability minimum percentage of cement, by weight is
explain: Standard mixes like 1:2:4 or M20 roughly result in a cement content around 15% by weight of the total mix.

q: 29. To indicate proper control of consistency of a freshly mixed concrete for pavement construction, the slump should be between
explain: Road concrete requires a very stiff mix (low workability) to ensure high strength and prevent flow; hence a low slump of 3-5 cm is used.

q: 30. The formula for calculating the depth of concrete pavements suggested by Goldbeck, is
explain: Goldbeck's formula for corner loading is d = √(3W/σ), where W is the wheel load and σ is the allowable stress.

q: 31. When load is applied on concrete pavement
options: away from edges, the maximum bending moment is negative
away from edges, the maximum bending moment cause compression
on the edges, the maximum stress is parallel to the edge
explain: Interior loading (away from edges) causes the slab to deflect like a dish, creating negative bending moments and tension at the bottom.

q: 32. For the design of cement concrete pavement for corner loading, Indian Road Congress recommends the use of
explain: While Westergaard is more theoretically complex, IRC historically used simplified versions like Goldbeck's for practical corner design.

q: 33. If d is the economic designed depth of a slab, the thickness of the cement concrete pavement slab at interior, is kept
explain: The interior of the slab experiences less stress than the corners/edges, so the thickness can be reduced to roughly 85% of the edge thickness.

q: 34. Reinforcement in cement concrete slab of road pavements, is placed
options: in the form of welded wire mesh
explain: Reinforcement is provided in both directions to control temperature cracks and distribute loads efficiently.

q: 35. Depth of reinforcement below the surface of a concrete pavement, is generally kept
explain: A standard cover of 5 cm is maintained to protect the steel from corrosion while remaining effective in resisting surface-level stresses.

q: 36. To prevent compressive stresses in a rigid concrete pavement, the joint provided, is
explain: Expansion joints allow the slab to lengthen during hot weather, preventing compressive buckling.

q: 37. Transverse joints are provided at distances varying from
explain: Modern spacing for expansion joints in rigid pavements typically falls in the 17m to 27m range, depending on temperature variation.

q: 38. Minimum thickness of a layer of fine sand required to cut off capillary rise of water completely, should be
explain: To completely break the capillary attraction in fine-grained soils, a thick sand blanket of about 76 cm is required.

q: 39. To prevent movement of moisture from subgrade to road pavement at the same level as that of water-table, thickness of a cut off layer of coarse sand, is
explain: Coarse sand has larger voids, making a thinner layer (15 cm) effective as a capillary cut-off compared to fine sand.

q: 40. Newly constructed pavement with ordinary Portland cement attains its working strength after
explain: Concrete is traditionally considered to have reached its full design strength at the 28-day curing mark.

q: 41. Pavement is said to be flexible if it contains
explain: Flexible pavements are those that deform under load and transmit pressure through grain-to-grain contact; WBM and bitumen layers fit this description.

q: 42. Design of flexible pavement, involves
explain: Designers must consider the magnitude of load, frequency of application (traffic), and environmental factors like rainfall and temperature.

q: 43. Design of flexible pavements is based on
options: a compromise of pure theory and empirical formula
explain: Most flexible pavement design methods (like CBR) are based on empirical observations and testing rather than rigid structural theory.

q: 44. California Bearing Ratio method of designing flexible pavements is more accurate as it involves
options: character of the road making materials
explain: The CBR test directly measures the resistance of the subgrade soil to penetration, which is the primary factor in flexible pavement thickness.

q: 45. Bottom-most component of a flexible pavement, is
explain: The subgrade is the prepared natural soil foundation upon which all other layers are built.

q: 46. Cement grouted pavement is classified as
explain: Because it uses a cement binder within a stone matrix but doesn't have the full structural slab action of PCC, it is called semi-rigid.

q: 47. Thickness of a pavement may be reduced considerably by
options: combination of all of the above
explain: Improving the strength of the subgrade through any of these methods allows for a thinner (and cheaper) upper pavement structure.

q: 48. Minimum thickness of the base of a flexible pavement is
explain: A standard minimum of 10 cm is required for the base layer to ensure proper load distribution and construction stability.

q: 49. For a poorly graded sub-grade soil, thickness of sub-base, is
explain: Poorly graded soils have low bearing capacity, requiring a thick sub-base layer (30 cm) to protect the subgrade.

q: 50. Design of highways is based on
explain: Pavement structural design is primarily governed by the weight transmitted through the axle loads (e.g., the 8160 kg standard axle).
